title: The Development and Validation of a Simple Method for the Determination of Meropenem Concentrations in Human Plasma Using High‐Performance Liquid Chromatography
content:
A simple, rapid, and sustainable HPLC-UV method was developed and validated to quantify meropenem in human plasma across a wide linear range (0.5–100 mg/L). Utilizing an efficient one-step protein precipitation, this eco-friendly approach is highly suited for routine clinical therapeutic drug monitoring and research purposes.


ABSTRACT

Meropenem is a beta-lactam antimicrobial that is used to treat severe infections. Critically ill patients are highly prone to pharmacokinetics variability and a fluctuation in meropenem plasma concentrations. The aim of this study is to provide a simple, rapid, precise and accurate method for the analysis of meropenem in human plasma using high-performance liquid chromatography. Sample preparation involved a single step deproteinization of plasma (0.2 mL) using cold methanol in a 2:1 ratio. Chromatographic separation was achieved on a C18 column using a mobile phase of 50 mM phosphate buffer (pH 6.5) and acetonitrile (90:10, vol/vol) at a flow rate of 1 mL/min, with a total run time of 15 min. Ultraviolet detection was performed at 300 nm for meropenem and 254 nm for caffeine (internal standard). The method demonstrated excellent linearity over the range of 0.5–100 mg/L (r2 > 0.99) with inter- and intra-day precision and accuracy within acceptable limits. Finally, environmental impact assessment using various greenness tools confirmed the method's sustainability. The developed method is a simple, rapid and accurate method that could be utilized for research and therapeutic drug monitoring purposes to measure meropenem concentrations in human plasma.
